title: Write a clarifying question someone else can answer
why_matters: Bad questions are open-ended and require your stakeholder to do all the work ("what are the requirements?"). Good questions are specific, answerable, and reveal what you've already done. The skill of asking a better question is the closest thing to a superpower in this role.
steps: Pick one thing you currently don't understand about your initiative. Write the lazy version of the question — the one you'd ask if you were in a hurry.
Now rewrite it three times. First: name what you've already tried to find out. Second: narrow it to a yes/no question or a multiple choice. Third: name the consequence of not having the answer.
Send the best version to the right person — in writing if they prefer email, in person if they don't.
Note their reaction time and the precision of their answer. Both tell you something about the question, not the person.
success_criteria: You have asked one written clarifying question and received an answer specific enough to act on. The before/after of your draft is saved in your private notes.
reflection_prompt: What changed between draft 1 and the version you sent? One sentence on the technique, one sentence on whether you'd use it again.
